newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP confirms Griffin oil field closes.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP confirms Griffin oil field closes.

text.p: Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd on Tuesday confirmed it has stopped production and disconnected the floating platform from the Griffin oil field to avoid the path of cyclone Rachel, which is bearing down on the Western Australia coast.

The platform, situated in the Indian Ocean, which was producing around 70,000 barrels of crude a day before a series of cyclones moved into the region, shut down as planned on Monday evening and began a westerly course earlier on Tuesday away from the cyclone, an official of BHP told Reuters.
"We hope to bring it back by the end of the week, but its still very unpredictable," the official, said.

The cyclone, which is expected to generate wind gust up to 200 kilometres per hour, should mover closer to the coastline and be in the vicinity of the ports of Karratha and Dampier late on Tuesday, the Bureau of Meteorology said.
The platform was recently disconnected from its mooring to escape the path of the previous cyclone Phil, which has since dissipated, and it was only reconnected last Friday,
BHP holds a 45-percent interest in the Griffin oil project and is the operator. Mobil Corp holds 35 percent and Inpex Alpha Ltd owns the remaining 20 percent.
Woodside Petroleum Ltd on Tuesday confirmed the Cossack Pioneer oil platform had disconnected from its offshore moooring in the Indian Ocean to flee the path of cyclone Rachel.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf are units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Woodside.
